getting-started.speaker: Ali Morrisane
getting-started.text: Good day and welcome back to Al Kharid.

getting-started.speaker: Ali Morrisane
getting-started.text: My name is Ali Morrisane - the greatest salesman in the world.

options.text: Are you really the greatest salesman in the world?

steps.player: If you're the greatest salesman in the world, why are you still selling goods from a stall?

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Well one can only do and sell so much. If I had more staff I'd be able to sell more, rather than wasting my time on menial things. I could get on with selling sand to the Bedabin and useless tourist trinkets to just about

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: everyone else.

options.text: I'm too busy to help. Adventuring is a full time job you know!

steps.player: I'm too busy to help. Adventuring is a full time job you know!

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: No problem my friend, perhaps another time.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Anyway, have a look at my wares.

options.text: No, I'm really too busy.
Okay.
I'd like to help you, but...

steps.player: I'd like to help you but...

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Yes, I know, I know - the life of a shop keeper isn't slaying dragons and wooing damsels, but it has its charms.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Although perhaps you can help me some other way. A nephew of mine lives not too far from here in a little town called Pollnivneach. He was supposed to become my assistant, but he hasn't shown up. If you fetch him

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: here I'll give you the first month of his salary!

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: I'll find your nephew.
But you had better become the greatest merchant in Gielinor once I succeed!

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Ah, many thanks, my friend. My nephew's name is Ali and he lives to the south in a town called Pollnivneach.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Tell him his uncle Ali M needs his help up in Al Kharid.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: And while you're here, have a look at my wares.

options.text: No, I'm really too busy.
Okay.
No.

steps.player: I'm too busy to help. Adventuring is a full time job you know!

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: No problem my friend, perhaps another time.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Anyway, have a look at my wares.

options.text: No, I'm really too busy.
Okay.
So what are you selling then?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.speaker: Ali Morrisane
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.text: I sent you to learn the whereabouts of my nephew, Ali. Is there any word of him in Pollnivneach?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.speaker: Ali Morrisane
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.text: That's not really the news I was hoping for.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.speaker: Ali Morrisane
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.text: But since you've been gone trade has gotten even busier. Will you have a look at my wares?

options.text: No, I'm really too busy.
Okay.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: Welcome, adventurer, to the town of Pollnivneach, the gateway to Menaphos and Al Kharid. My name is Ali and I'm the mayor of this town. I hope you enjoy your stay here.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.player: Thank you. That is one of the warmest welcomes I've ever had! People generally treat travelling adventurers with suspicion.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: All are welcome here. Now more than ever I suppose.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.player: What do you mean by that?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: There's trouble in town, and a lot of villagers have left as a result. Things are looking dire.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.player: I'm looking for someone called Ali.
I mean I'm looking for a specific Ali. He's Ali Morrisane's nephew.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: Oh, that Ali! Well, er, your best bet is to ask around town. I'm sure someone will know what he's up to.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-cam.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-cam.text: Welcome to my discount camel store. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: A discount camel store?

steps.player: A discount camel store?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Yes - it's my great idea - selling camels at discounted prices so that the common man can experience the joys of owning a camel of their very own! They're not just a source of kebab meat you know!

options.text: So can I buy a camel then? I'm hungry!

steps.player: So can I buy a camel then? I'm hungry!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I would never sell one to the likes of you! They are beautiful, majestic creatures, not food! Get out of my shop.

options.text: Yes, camels are beautiful creatures.

steps.player: Yes, camels are beautiful creatures.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Ah, wondrous camels! Best of all Saradomin's creations. Ships of the desert, far more useful than any horse or donkey. Truly, they are a man's best friend.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Perhaps you'd like a camel of your own? You're in the right place, if so...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Well yes, actually I would like to ask about something else.
No, but thanks for your time.

steps.player: No, but thanks for your time.

options.text: Why would I want a camel? All they do is spit and...

steps.player: Why would I want a camel? All they do is spit and...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Pah! I've seen mummies with more brains than you! If you treat camels badly then of course they're going to spit at you. May your robes never be clean again!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Actually, I think I was a camel in a previous life.

steps.player: Actually, I think I was a camel in a previous life.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: You're teasing me now! You rogue!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Everyone laughs at the poor Discount Camel Seller.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: So is the discount camel business good then?

steps.player: So is the discount camel business good then?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Business is booming! Pollnivneach has never seen this number of visitors.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: In fact I'm thinking of expanding and trying to break into the camel hire market.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: If only I could figure out how to get people to return the camels...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Tell me about this town.

steps.player: Tell me about this town.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well, Pollnivneach is a funny little place. It's a small town and you'd think it'd be nice and quiet.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: But those Menaphites and bandits are making the place quite unbearable.

options.text: In what way?

steps.player: In what way?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well, one group is as bad as the other! They steal, they fight, they cause trouble with us locals. Just yesterday one of those bandits came looking for protection money!

steps.player: Why don't the authorities stop this?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: We're a small town. We don't have the resources to keep the gangs off our backs! Menaphos and Al Kharid are no help either.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: To tell the truth we live in hope that an outsider, someone with no ties to either group, could broker a deal to halt the hostilities between them.

steps.player: Hmm...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Well the weak will always be trodden on. Why not stand up to them?

steps.player: Well the weak will always be trodden on. Why not stand up to them?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: That's a little unfair, my friend. We can't all be brave adventurers. If we were, where would you purchase quality camels at discounted prices?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: You might think about that. Anyway, isn't it the job of the brave adventurer to protect the weak and innocent from evil and harm?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Perhaps I could help.

steps.player: Perhaps I could help.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Yes, perhaps you could.

steps.player: You know the politics better than I do. What do you recommend?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Me?! I am but a humble discount camel seller. You're the adventurer, don't you know what to do?

options.text: Of course I know what to do! I was just testing you!

steps.player: Of course I know what to do! I was just testing you!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: That is reassuring to hear. Too often one meets brainless adventurers whose solution to every problem is to hack, maim and murder.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I'm glad to know you're not of that ilk.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Perhaps I should know, but offered advice should never be shunned.

steps.player: Perhaps I should know, but offered advice should never be shunned.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: The state of adventurers today. They need everything spelled out for them.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: What, you want me to put a little note in your quest journal?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: But fine, I'll give you a hint. Try and see if you can get the gangs to agree to a truce by offering them each a token gift as an act of reconciliation.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: If that fails to work, you must consider trying to influence the gangs from within.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Lovely day isn't it?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: It's a beautiful day today, but word has it that it will rain tomorrow.

steps.player: Really?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: No! When have you ever known it to rain here in Gielinor?

steps.player: Oh. Anyway...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Are those camels around the side for sale?

steps.player: Are those camels around the side for sale?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Those two camels around the side are already sold.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I've got new stock coming very soon though. Come back later if you're still interested.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Well yes, actually I would like to ask about something else.
No, but thanks for your time.

steps.player: No, but thanks for your time.

options.text: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.player: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well, you've found your man.

steps.player: Really? Do you have an uncle called Ali?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Why yes - all my uncles are called Ali!

steps.player: Oh dear! Do any of them own a stall in the Al Kharid Bazaar?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well no, but one of them owns a moderately successful camel hire franchise.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Have you considered hiring a camel? Or perhaps purchasing one of your own? I can get you a discount.

steps.player: Never mind.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-rug-mer.speaker: Rug Merchant
asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-rug-mer.text: Greetings, desert traveller. Do you require the services of Ali Morrisane's flying carpet fleet?

options.text: Yes please.
Tell me about Ali Morrisane.

steps.player: Tell me about Ali Morrisane.

steps.speaker: Rug Merchant
steps.text: What, you haven't heard of Ali M? Possibly the greatest salesman of the Kharidian empire if not all Gielinor?

steps.player: Hold on... yes I can place him now. He has me looking for his nephew Ali, I think he needs some help with his shop.

steps.speaker: Rug Merchant
steps.text: I wouldn't be surprised, he's mentioned to me on a few occasions that he is thinking of diversifying even further.

steps.player: You wouldn't have seen his nephew about then?

steps.speaker: Rug Merchant
steps.text: No it's been a quite a while since I last saw him.

options.text: Tell me about this magic carpet fleet.
I have some questions.
No thanks.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.speaker: Street urchin
asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.text: No one knows what's going on in the streets better than me. I live, sleep, eat and drink here. The fact that I'm so small means that people tend to ignore me which helps even more.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.speaker: Street urchin
asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.text: Do you need any other information?

options.text: Yes tell me about...

steps.player: Yes, tell me about...

options.text: The Menaphites

steps.player: Tell me about the Menaphites.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: They're a bad bunch, always starting fights down in the Asp and Snake. Word on the street is that they're led by some deranged priest. Nobody's ever seen them though - they do all their deals through Ali 'the

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Operator'. I reckon they're up to something, but they're such a close knit group that little ever slips out.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

options.text: The bandits

steps.player: Tell me about the bandits.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: There's not much to say, really. They're just a group of local thugs led by the biggest and strongest amongst them. If they have any other plans, I don't know about it.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

options.text: The Mayor

steps.player: Tell me about the Mayor.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: The mayor is a spineless coward! He never stands up to anybody. That's why the Menaphites are so strong now! He let them stay, and then they started causing trouble. When he realised his mistake, he hired a band

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: of local thugs to drive them out, but they saw how weak he was and turned on us too. Now we've got bandits and Menaphites, and the mayor isn't doing anything!

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

options.text: Ali Morrisane's nephew

steps.player: Tell me about Ali Morrisane's nephew.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: I know him! He used to kick us when he caught any of us stealing from his stall.

steps.player: Do you know where he is now then?

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: He disappeared a little while ago. All I know is it had something to do with the gangs. Probably he scammed them. You'd have to gain their trust to find out more, m'afraid - if I get too close, they might disappear me

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: too!

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

options.text: The town

steps.player: Tell me about the town.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: It's boring! We're not as big as Menaphos or as powerful as Al Kharid, and we've got a really nasty crime problem. It's no wonder so many grown-ups have left.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

options.text: No thanks.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-ali-the.speaker: Ali the Barman
asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-ali-the.text: Good day. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, I'd like a drink please.

steps.player: Yes, I'd like a drink please.

options.text: What's going on in town?

steps.player: What's going on in town?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Nothing much really. About what you'd expect from a sleepy little town like ours.

steps.player: What about those two gangs? That seems exciting.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: They're paying customers, so I won't rock the boat if you don't mind.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: No thanks, I'm ok.

steps.player: No thanks, I'm ok. Thanks for your time.

options.text: Yes, I'd like to talk about something else.
I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.player: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Well, I'm called Ali and I'm from here. Are you looking for me?

steps.player: Do you have an uncle called Ali?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Yes! All my uncles are called Ali!

steps.player: Oh dear. Well do any of your uncles have a stall in the Bazaar in Al Kharid?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Um... no.

steps.player: Well do you know if anyone here does?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: That's a difficult question to answer. I don't know anyone else's uncles.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

steps.player: The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Maybe around these parts. Were you expecting it to have 'Ali' in the name?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: I did think about calling it 'Ali's', but then it'd get confused with the Camel Shop, the Kebab House, the Mayor's residence...

steps.player: Yes, I get your point. It's a perfectly fine name.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Ahh, a kind stranger. Get this old man a drink so that he may wet his throat and tell you of the strange happenings in this town.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Now where were we? Ah yes, Ali Morrisane's wayward nephew.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: What?! How did you know that's who I was looking for?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Er... well, he's a real scamp, that lad! I can't imagine a stranger would be asking after anyone else.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Hmm. Well go on then, where is he?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: I'd tell you more, but my throat is drying up. This desert climate is an inhospitable one. Get me another beer so that I can continue my tale.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Get this poor, thirsty old man another drink so that he may wet his lips and continue.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: You are too kind, now what were we talking about?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Of course! I've known him since he was a wee lad. A right little mischievous beggar...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Yes, I can imagine. Do you have any more recent information about him? Where is he?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Well now, if you had just asked me that in the first place I would have told you directly!

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: You're right, I'm sorry for beating around the bush. Do you know where Ali's nephew is now, though?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: I'd tell you more, but my throat is drying up. This desert climate is an inhospitable one. Get me another beer so that I can continue my tale.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Alas, my throat has dried up, and I cannot speak... perhaps another drink would help?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Ahh, that hits the spot.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Now which of you two adventurers wanted to know where Ali's nephew is?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Is this a double? No wonder I feel sick...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Look, all I want to know is the whereabouts of Ali Morrisane's nephew.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Now is that his nephew from his side or his wife's? They have a huge family you see. I remember...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: No, no, no. Stop right there. You are not going to fool me into buying you another beer without first giving me some useful information.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: But my lips are so dry, how can I possibly continue?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Well if your lips are dry, I'll have to wring you like a wet cloth and squeeze out enough booze to fill another tankard. I'd reckon it would hurt though.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: I see. Don't worry about me, I'll just have to soldier on. Now what do you want to know?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: For the last time, where is Ali Morrisane's nephew?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Oh, I don't know.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Wait, wait! The last I heard he was in trouble with those gangs hanging around town. You won't get any answers out of them, though, not while they're feuding. Maybe if you were to solve that little problem...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Anyway, is there any chance of another beer?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: What were we talking about again? Yes yes, when I was a boy... no, that's not it.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Eh? What's this? I don't want that, get me a beer.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.player: I am trying to get to the bottom of this feud between you and the Menaphites.
I'm just trying to understand why thieves of your repute would stoop to their level.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.speaker: Bandit
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.text: Well, if memory serves me correctly, I think the hostilities began when they robbed one of our camels. A heinous crime.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.player: So if they offered a camel back as a gesture of goodwill, would you and the rest of the bandits cease your hostilities?

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.speaker: Bandit
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.text: Those Menaphites would never do that. They have no sense of honour.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.player: I am trying to figure out the feud that exists between you and the Bandits.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: Not much to figure out there, the problem is those thieving bandits.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: They are always stealing, starting fights and disrupting the lives of the townsfolk.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.player: Word has it that the Menaphites are also involved in unsavoury behaviour.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: Well, we also steal, start fights, and disrupt lives - but we do it with class! And the bandits definitely started it.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: I can scarcely remember, it's been so long.

steps.text: A rather loud clank reverberates from the safe. It sounds as if you've gotten the combination wrong. You wonder how many more attempts you have before the safe permanently locks itself.
Clank!! That must be the safe resetting itself.
If the player has a full inventory:
The mayor's jewels are contained within the safe, however you have no room in your inventory to take them.
Otherwise:
You remove the jewels from the safe.

now-you-ve-stolen-the-jewels-talking-to-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
now-you-ve-stolen-the-jewels-talking-to-.text: I really can't chat for very long, the recent escalation in crime has me run off my feet. Just a short while ago even my own house was robbed. This cannot continue.

now-you-ve-stolen-the-jewels-talking-to-.speaker: Ali the Operator
now-you-ve-stolen-the-jewels-talking-to-.text: Impressive, I didn't expect you to crack that safe so quickly. Did you have help?

now-you-ve-stolen-the-jewels-talking-to-.player: Of course not, although the mayor did leave a number of hints lying around.

now-you-ve-stolen-the-jewels-talking-to-.speaker: Ali the Operator
now-you-ve-stolen-the-jewels-talking-to-.text: That man is a fool. Now give me the jewels.
If the player does not have the jewels:

steps.player: Actually I seem to have misplaced them.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: You are trying my patience. Hurry back with the jewels. Don't disappoint me.
You hand Ali the Operator the jewels.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Now, your final task is one of the upmost importance. It has come to my attention that there is a traitor in our midst.

steps.player: Oh really?

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Yes, and I want you to root them out.

steps.player: Why me?

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Because I feel like I can trust you. You don't have the emotional baggage that comes with playing the villain your entire life.

steps.player: Aw! You can count on me to find the traitor.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Well then get to it.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: How is the search for the traitor going?

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: Make sure you interview our other members. They may know more than they let on.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: Can I help you with anything else?

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.player: I was wondering if you could help me?

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.speaker: Menaphite Thug
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.text: Tell me what your problem is and I'll see what I can do.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.player: I've heard there's a traitor among the Menaphites. What do you know about it?
Really? So what do you know?

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.speaker: Menaphite Thug
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.text: I just can't believe one of my friends could be a traitor.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.speaker: Menaphite Thug
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.text: Well, I suppose there is Traitorous Ali.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.speaker: Menaphite Thug
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.text: Oh yes. The most untrustworthy, backstabbing little rat to scamper across Tumeken's fair desert. He'd sell his own mother to slavers if he hadn't already betrayed her and had her locked up for the last job he pulled.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.player: I suppose the name is a bit of a giveaway.
That was a little too simple, are you sure it was him?

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.speaker: Menaphite Thug
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.text: Positive, he was turned by the offer of a set of waterproofs and a ride on a camel.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.player: I see he drives a hard bargain.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.speaker: Menaphite Thug
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-a-m.text: Well what can I say? We don't call him 'Ali of the Good Decisions', do we?

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.player: I have discovered the identity of the traitor. It was...

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: No! I would never have suspected Traitorous Ali.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: Well, there was that time he sold out his entire family for a sandpit and an umbrella.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: But I'm sure it took much more for him to betray us!

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.player: Actually he sold you out for...

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: Stop, I don't want to know. It hurts too much already. Find him and then kill him, but do it quietly. I don't want a fuss.

searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Operator
searching-for-the-traitor-talking-to-ali.text: Can I help you with anything else?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-ope.speaker: Ali the Operator
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-ope.text: Well don't waste time talking to me. Get on with it.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-bar.speaker: Ali the Barman
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-bar.text: Good day. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, I'd like a drink please.
What's going on in town?
I'm looking for Traitorous Ali.

steps.player: I'm looking for Traitorous Ali.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: He was just here! Look, he's even left his drink on the table by those barrels. Must have nipped out to go to the toilet.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: He might be gone a while though. The nearest outhouse is all the way over on Fossil Island.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: No thanks, I'm ok.

steps.player: No thanks, I'm ok. Thanks for your time.

options.text: Yes, I'd like to talk about something else.
I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.
The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Good day to you too, Blockhead.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Now what do you want? A hex? A spot potion? Power, beauty, eternal youth, etcetera?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: Actually I just want your help to, erm, remove someone. It's simple enough!

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Ahh, I see. But I warn you, stranger - extinguishing the flame of life is simple, but people rarely wish to face the consequences, and I doubt you are any different.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: Don't worry about the consequences - I need it carried out in a manner which would draw no suspicion to me.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Well now this is getting interesting. I'd recommend a poisoning. Who do you wish dead? I need to know so that I may tailor a poison to their specific needs.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Traitorous Ali? Say no more! That wretch traded his grandmother's house for a jar of pickled aubergines! I believe he'll be easily gotten rid of...

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: None at all - I will extract much pleasure from his passing. Just bring me the ingredients I require.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Ah, impatience! Traitorous Ali's time is indeed nigh. Firstly bring me some snake venom, which will act as the main toxin.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: Where would I get some snake poison?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: From a snake perhaps?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: What I meant was how do I extract the poison from the snake?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Sheesh! You'd make a terrible hag. Just bring me a snake with teeth in its head - and don't even think of giving me that snake charmer's pet worm, it's about as dangerous as a rubber knife.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Good day to you too, Blockhead.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Have you got a snake yet?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: No, I'm still working on that.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Well don't bother me again until you do!

steps.text: Your snake charming skills are insufficient to pacify the creature.
You successfully charm and capture the snake!

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Good day to you too, Blockhead.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: I have the snake. What else do you need?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Ah yes, that snake will do nicely. Hello, you wriggly little cutie!

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Who's a vindictive little beast? You are! You are!

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: Erm, yes. Do you need anything else?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Now that I have the toxin I need something to hide its trace. Fresh camel dung should do the job.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Do you want the poison or not?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: Fine, fine, I'll get some camel dung.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: And make that fresh camel dung! Nice and stinky. Now hand over that venomous little darling before it takes a bite out of you.
You hand the basket with the charmed snake over to the old hag.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Good day to you too, Blockhead.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Do you have the camel dung yet?

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: No, I'm still working on that.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Well don't come back until you have it!

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Good day to you too, Blockhead.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Here's your poison!

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Actually I already had it brewing. I just needed the ingredients for another batch.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: You wouldn't believe the demand. It's been murder!

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Sorry, I've been dying to say that for ages.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.player: Just stop. Thanks for the poison and good day to you.

planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.speaker: Ali the Hag
planning-a-murder-talking-to-ali-the-hag.text: Wait! Just remember, this poison isn't designed to be used on a weapon. In fact it's not a contact poison at all. You'll have to do more than just smear it on a blade!
You hand over your bucket of fresh camel dung and receive a vial of poison in return.

the-end-of-traitorous-ali-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Hag
the-end-of-traitorous-ali-talking-to-ali.text: Good day to you too, Blockhead.

the-end-of-traitorous-ali-talking-to-ali.player: I was wondering if I could have another batch of poison?

the-end-of-traitorous-ali-talking-to-ali.speaker: Ali the Hag
the-end-of-traitorous-ali-talking-to-ali.text: Why? Was the first batch not good enough?
If the player has the Hag's poison in their inventory:

steps.player: Well no, I was just being greedy and wanted another batch for no good reason.

steps.speaker: Ali the Hag
steps.text: Well if that's the case, no! I have better things to be doing than continuously brewing poisons for people who have no use for it.

steps.player: I lost the first batch.

steps.speaker: Ali the Hag
steps.text: What? How do you just lose a batch of the most potent poison in all of Gielinor? It's even more deadly than the jungle karambwan.

steps.player: It's a long and not very interesting story.

steps.speaker: Ali the Hag
steps.text: Well alright, I'll give you another batch this once.
(The player receives another Hag's poison.)

the-end-of-traitorous-ali-using-an-item-.player: I've poisoned the drink. I'd better leave it alone now in case someone notices.

reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.speaker: Ali the Hag
reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.text: Good day to you too, Blockhead.

reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.speaker: Ali the Hag
reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.text: Have you good reason to disturb me again?

reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.speaker: Ali the Hag
reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.text: I warned you about needlessly bothering me. That's it! I'm turning you into a frog!

reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.speaker: Ali the Hag
reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-ha.text: Don't taunt me, fool! Once I find a spare minute you'll be ribbiting on the other side of your face, you mark my words!

reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-op.player: Almost, his drink is poisoned. As soon as he gets back, he'll be done for.

reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-op.speaker: Ali the Operator
reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-op.text: Excellent work! Now, go speak with our boss.

reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-op.speaker: Ali the Operator
reporting-the-deed-talking-to-ali-the-op.text: He wants to discuss the future direction of the gang.

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-ali-the-op.player: I haven't spoken with him yet.

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.player: Ali the Operator said you wanted to see me.

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: That's right. I have kept a close eye on your progress. I'm impressed.

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.player: So what are your plans for the bandits?

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: The bandits? A mere nuisance, insignificant to my overall goal.

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.player: Wait, if you're not warring with the bandits, what are you planning?

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: World domination! First Pollnivneach, then Al Kharid, then the whole of the desert!

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: You do understand who we are, don't you?

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.player: Actually I thought you were a ragtag band of good-for- nothing thieves sucking the life out of this innocent town.

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: Silence! We are the descendants of assassins, the heirs of the revolutionaries who defeated the corrupt pharaoh and his brood!

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: For centuries we have wandered the desert, rebuilding the empire we were promised!

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: Will you join us in our quest to defeat the thralls of Tumeken and reclaim our birthright?
If the player has not completed Beneath Cursed Sands:

steps.player: Sorry, I have this irrational hatred for megalomaniac, despotic zealots! Prepare to meet your maker, you big jerk!

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: If the player has completed Beneath Cursed Sands:

steps.player: Wait, your great-great-great-great-grandparents were the ones who killed Osmumten?

steps.speaker: Menaphite Leader
steps.text: Who?

steps.player: You don't even know his name, and you claim to be the heirs to his empire? Come on.
You're just a bunch of petty tyrants looking for an excuse to hurt people.

steps.speaker: Menaphite Leader
steps.text: Be careful what you say! We are loyal servants of the Devourer!

steps.player: I hope so, because you're about to meet her in person. This is for Mehhar!

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-the-menaph.text: Fool! You'll never get to me. Guards protect me.
The Menaphite Leader summons the Tough Guy to attack the player.

meeting-the-leader-talking-to-a-menaphit.speaker: Menaphite Thug
meeting-the-leader-talking-to-a-menaphit.text: You treacherous jackal! Prepare to die!
The Menaphite Thug attacks the player.

meeting-the-leader-after-defeating-the-t.speaker: Menaphite Leader
meeting-the-leader-after-defeating-the-t.text: You haven't seen the last of me!

meeting-the-leader-after-defeating-the-t.player: No doubt I haven't seen the last of you... but what about Ali's nephew?
Maybe the villagers will feel more talkative now that I've rid them of these evil Menaphites. Who knows, they might even give me a reward!

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-me.speaker: Menaphite Thug
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-me.text: You treacherous jackal! I should never have trusted you.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-me.player: What can I say, you live and learn.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-me.text: The Menaphite Thug attacks the player.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-st.speaker: Street urchin
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-st.text: Hi! Do you want to go rob some more people? I could do with some more money.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-st.player: I think I need to try a different tactic. Sorry, kid!

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-st.speaker: Street urchin
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-st.text: Well do you need any information then?

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-st.player: No thanks, I think I have a fair idea of what is going on in the town now.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.text: I don't know what we did to deserve your presence here, but I for one am filled with regret.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.player: Well that's some show of gratitude! Can't I even get a 'thank you' for ridding your town of one of the gangs?

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.text: Do you understand the concept of consequences?

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.text: Well, the consequences of your little piece of butchery are that the town is now even worse off. The bandits no longer have to waste time and energy fighting with the Menaphites and can direct all their attention

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.text: towards making us miserable. So for your efforts I thank you, but I wish no-one had asked for your help.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.player: I'll set this town right before I leave, I promise.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.text: Why do I wish that you hadn't said that? Your heavyhanded tactics scare me.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-ba.speaker: Bandit
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-ba.text: It was brilliant the way you got rid of the Menaphite leader.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-ba.speaker: Bandit
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-ba.text: So will you run the rest of them out of town now?

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-the-.speaker: Cowardly Bandit
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-the-.text: Welcome. Our leader would be pleased to congratulate you on your disposal of the Menaphites who plagued this town.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.speaker: Ali the Operator
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-ali-.text: Why did you have to go and ruin everything? We had a beautiful future ahead of us, the town would have been ours!

options.text: Maybe I wanted to make it MY town!

steps.player: Maybe I wanted to make it MY town!

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: I see. I knew the hunger for power would get to you eventually.

options.text: Evil megalomaniacs set on destruction should be opposed.

steps.player: Evil megalomaniacs set on destruction should be opposed.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Really? I thought you were meant to follow those types blindly, with unquestioning loyalty.

steps.player: Look, Gielinor is full of power mad evil-doers. I'm sure another will come along soon enough.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: No... it just wouldn't be the same. I think I'll just wallow in self pity for a while.

options.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to upset you. Can we still be friends?

steps.player: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to upset you. Can we still be friends?

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: No, I think I'll just wallow in self pity for a while.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.speaker: Villager
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.text: You! You're the one that just made everything worse for us poor villagers!

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.player: What?! I just single-handedly took apart one of the gangs that was ruining your town!

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.speaker: Villager
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.text: You adventurers! You never think, you just act. You think that by killing a powerful bad person, Gielinor will become a better place.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.speaker: Villager
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.text: It's not that simple, things never are. You've created a vacuum, and now all that power will go to whoever's strong enough to take it.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.speaker: Villager
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.text: Who do you think is stronger? Our elderly mayor, or the leader of the bandits?

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.player: Oops. Sorry, I was just trying to help. So are things really that much worse?

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.speaker: Villager
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.text: Yes. Before your intervention the two gangs pretty much cancelled each other out. They spent most of their energy trying to kill each other.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.speaker: Villager
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.text: Now that the balance is lost, the Bandits reign unopposed! They no longer have to deal with the Menaphites and heap misery upon misery on us. You must finish the job that you have started.

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.player: You know, this adventuring lark is a lot more complicated than I thought!

celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.speaker: Villager
celebrating-your-victory-talking-to-a-vi.text: If you're prepared to change something you must also be prepared to deal with the consequences! Now hurry up and fix this mess you created!

options.text: What do you mean by fix the mess I created?

steps.player: What do you mean by fix the mess I created?

steps.speaker: Villager
steps.text: Do I have to spell it out to you?

steps.player: Would you please?

steps.speaker: Villager
steps.text: Just run the bandits out of town. Incidentally, I spotted their leader to the north-west just a few minutes ago.

options.text: Ok I'll get to it.

steps.player: Okay, I'll get to it.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.speaker: Bandit
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.text: Welcome! Our leader wants to congratulate you on your swift disposal of the Menaphites who plagued this town.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.text: Come here my friend, so I may embrace you. You have done us a great turn by disposing of those Menaphites.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.player: Don't jump to conclusions, I didn't do it for you.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.text: Regardless, I am still very grateful. Now I have the town at my mercy.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.player: That's what I'm here to talk to you about.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.text: Do you want a reward? A fee? I will not begrudge you that.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.player: No, I'm here to give you an ultimatum: either leave the town of your own free will or I will make you.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.text: How the worm has turned. This no-name adventurer who was robbing, looting and poisoning not too long ago is now taking the moral high ground! Or are you trying to keep the whole town for yourself?

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-talking-.text: Pollnivneach is mine. You won't run me out without a fight. If you want us gone, you must defeat our strongest warrior in battle.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.player: I have defeated your champion, now get out of town.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.text: Adventurer... I have underestimated you. Perhaps we can come to an agreement. How about I work for you? Think of the riches you would make.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.player: Don't try my patience. Tell me where Ali is, and then get out of here?
Ali Morrisane's nephew! I know you gangs had something to do with his disappearance, so tell me where he is!

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.text: Ali Morrisane?! You fool. You've been had!

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.speaker: Bandit Leader
running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.text: Go have a chat with these precious townspeople of yours. You'll soon learn the truth.

running-the-bandits-out-of-town-upon-def.player: I'll go talk to a villager now, just to prove you wrong. Now get out of here before I really get angry with you!

finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.player: I told you to clear off! Why are you still here?

finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.speaker: Bandit Leader
finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.text: Adventurer... I have underestimated you. Perhaps we can come to an agreement. How about I work for you? Think of the riches you would make.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.player: Don't try my patience. Get out of here, and never return to this town again!

finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.speaker: Bandit Leader
finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.text: Ha! You fancy yourself the people's champion, do you? You are so naive. You don't even realise you've been tricked!

finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.speaker: Bandit Leader
finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.text: Go have a chat with these precious townspeople of yours. You'll soon see.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-bandit-leade.player: I'll go talk to a villager now, just to prove you wrong. Now get out of here before I really get angry with you.

finishing-up-talking-to-a-bandit.speaker: Bandit
finishing-up-talking-to-a-bandit.text: You dog! You killed our champion and for that you will die!

finishing-up-talking-to-the-cowardly-ban.speaker: Cowardly Bandit
finishing-up-talking-to-the-cowardly-ban.text: You dog! You killed our champion and for that I hope you die a slow and painful death.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-cowardly-ban.player: What was that? Are you looking for a fight?

finishing-up-talking-to-the-cowardly-ban.speaker: Cowardly Bandit
finishing-up-talking-to-the-cowardly-ban.text: Me? No, no, I was just, er, complimenting your, that is - don't kill me, please!

finishing-up-talking-to-a-villager.player: I have delivered you from two evil tyrants. Where's my thank you?

finishing-up-talking-to-a-villager.speaker: Villager
finishing-up-talking-to-a-villager.text: Thank you? For what? You come into our town. You rob, mug, burgle and kill and then expect respect and gratitude? Look, if it's praise and thanks you're looking for, talk to the mayor.

finishing-up-talking-to-a-villager.player: I wonder why I bother sometimes! This place has been nothing but trouble and I still haven't found Ali's nephew.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: My thanks, adventurer. Your methods and motives may be questionable, but none can argue that you have delivered our little town from the wicked gangs who plagued it. I think things will change around here, now

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: that our problems are at a manageable size.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: The least that I can do for you is answer your questions about the whereabouts of Ali Morrisane's nephew. He always was a mischievous young man, full of harebrained schemes.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: He dreamed of being the greatest salesman in all of Gielinor! Unfortunately, he was a little too good.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: He angered a number of people by coercing them into buying things they didn't really want. Completely within the law, of course, but the law could only protect young Ali for so long.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: Once he angered the Menaphites and the bandits, I knew I could no longer protect him.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: Under cover of darkness I smuggled him out of the town, and he's been gone ever since.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: I can assure you, however, that he is safe and well - and now that you have effectively ended the threat posed by the gangs, he can continue his business elsewhere. Last I heard he planned to open some kind

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: of trade network with forty of his friends. A 'treasure trove', he claims. I'll believe it when I see it.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: I hope that helps you in your quest. If you speak to Ali Morrisane, do tell him that I wholeheartedly apologise for the way he - er, his family - has been treated.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.player: I think I may be able to help with one other thing. I heard that your house was burgled recently. If you're interested in recovering the goods, you ought to have a word with Ali the Operator.

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: Now, how would a passing adventurer know where to find my missing jewels?

finishing-up-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.player: Er, let's just put it down to adventurer's intuition.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Thank you once again. Have you spoken to Ali Morrisane yet?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: No not yet.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Mayor
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Perhaps you should! I'm sure he's keen to hear word of his nephew.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Hello there.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Barman
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Good day. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, I'd like a drink please.
What's going on in town?

steps.player: What's going on in town?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Well since you gave the two gangs a good kicking, business has really taken off! Both gangs are spending all their gold here drowning their sorrows.

steps.player: That's great! So do I get a cut of the profits?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Get out of here, you cheeky rascal. A cut of my profits? As if!

options.text: The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

steps.player: The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Maybe around these parts. Were you expecting it to have 'Ali' in the name?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: I did think about calling it 'Ali's', but then it'd get confused with the Camel Shop, the Kebab House, the Mayor's residence...

steps.player: Yes, I get your point. It's a perfectly fine name.

options.text: Could you tell Traitorous Ali that someone has poisoned his drink?

steps.player: Could you tell Traitorous Ali that someone has poisoned his drink?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: What?! Poisoned drinks, in my bar?! My reputation would be destroyed if someone died here. Thank you adventurer.

steps.player: No problem at all.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Here, have a beer - it's on the house.

options.text: Thanks!

steps.text: Ali the barman gives you a beer.

options.text: Thanks but no thanks, I don't drink.

steps.player: Thanks but no thanks, I don't drink.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Don't say that around here too loud please, it may catch and then I'd be out of business.

steps.player: You could always open up a non alcoholic fruit juice bar. You'd have less problems with drunken customers

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: You might be onto something there, but then what would I do with the drunken sailor?

steps.player: Who?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Drunken Ali. Oh never mind it's a long story.

options.text: Yuck! I don't like beer.

steps.player: Yuck! I don't like beer.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Fine, suit yourself. There's no need to insult me.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Hello there.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Barman
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Good day. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, I'd like a drink please.
What's going on in town?
The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Hello! Welcome back to my discount camel store. How are those camels getting along?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Hey Ali!

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Hello adventurer.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Any news?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Not much really, I just want to thank you for what you have done for this town. I might even stick around now that business is better!

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Any grand plans?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Well I've been debating whether I should diversify into camel rental, too. Although I do have all these cages lying around... do you think there's a market for discount jackals?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Maybe! Best of luck, in any case.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Thank you.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Hello again my friend. I have heard nothing from my troublesome nephew. Have you any news of his whereabouts?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Indeed I do. I was able to eventually learn of his fortunes, although it was a little bit more challenging than I originally thought.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Well then please, tell me what has become of him. Nothing bad I hope.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: I was able to discover that he is quite the salesman. Perhaps too good. He has roughly forty people working under him.
Unfortunately a number of people didn't approve of his sales techniques and as a result he is in hiding.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: You make an old man very happy. I'm so proud of young Baba.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: But he's considered a thief!

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Yes, by people with too much money and not enough sense. All willingly parted with their money and received what they purchased.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Well, it seems I still am in need of an assistant...

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: ..but take the reward anyway.
Ali Morrisane gives you 500 coins.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: I've just been thinking Ali, there seems to be a few parallels between yourself and your nephew. Both of you are unscrupulous salesmen, both of you come from the same town and both of you no longer trade there.
Were you sent into exile too?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: I have my reasons.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: No, now hang on, this seems to me like one of the strangest quests I have ever been involved with. I do not believe that a businessman like you would not know of a competitor, particularly a competitor as talented as
your nephew.
So what was your motive to get me to visit Pollnivneach? Was it concern for the towns people? Hmm. I don't think so, I'd say you would probably sell your grandmother if you could get a good price for
her. What was the reason?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: My my, you surprise me, you're not as dumb as you look.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Surely you didn't do all this to sell me a fake beard and headpiece.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Ah, once again you underestimate me. I sold you far more than that.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: Really? Well I did buy some other odds and ends off you.... no hang on! I get it now, you're in league with Ali the Camel seller, the Kebab seller and the mayor aren't you.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: I like the word 'tourism'. Did you not enjoy your stay in Pollnivneach? Was there not action, intrigue and fun to be had, and did you not notice all the other tourists there too?

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.player: I must apologise for ever doubting you. You really are the greatest salesman in all of Gielinor.

reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.speaker: Ali Morrisane
reporting-back-to-ali-morrisane-talking-.text: Now that we both agree on that, may I show you my wares?

options.text: No, I'm really too busy.

steps.text: Quest complete!

options.text: Okay.

nIVxya.speaker: Street urchin
nIVxya.text: Come back if you need any info about anything in the town.

SckW-U.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
SckW-U.text: I would consider giving them to you if you were able to look after them. But it is abundantly clear that you've got your hands - and your inventory - full at the moment.

uxwUE4.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
uxwUE4.text: You don't even have that much money do you? Come back when you're able to make a proper offer and stop wasting my time.
